recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore Request.requester.agent/onBehalfOf without a new work-group decision reversing the later PractitionerRole-based workflow pattern.
issue_request: FHIR-11424 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2 and requested changing Request.requester from a single Reference to a backbone with requester.agent 1..1 and requester.onBehalfOf 0..1 Organization, constrained so onBehalfOf only applies for Practitioner or Device agents.
initial_application: The 2016 workflow batch commit 839bf586d6c1cf9a322e122852f0cc49bcfed263 applied the requested Request.requester.agent/onBehalfOf structure and invariant. Later workflow-pattern history intentionally changed that representation: FHIR-13159/SVN#12374 in commit 5064224bd079b7f4ef4023d3ead9111b57bd8bff made Request.requester a direct Reference including PractitionerRole, and commit 14b69a1c6dd33918b20d53ffd6cfbab523f840ba removed the stale onBehalfOf invariant.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request as an active logical model, and the current Request spreadsheet defines Request.requester as Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization|Patient|RelatedPerson|Device). FHIR-13159 and FHIR-15128 are already represented on the combined branch; they establish and preserve the PractitionerRole-based workflow-pattern direction rather than restoring onBehalfOf.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build input already supports identifying a practitioner acting for an organization through PractitionerRole, so reintroducing Request.requester.agent/onBehalfOf would contradict later final decisions.
